newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU gives final okay to Global One telecoms deal.
newsitem.headline: EU gives final okay to Global One telecoms deal.

text.p: The European Commission gave final approval on Tuesday to the Global One telecommunications alliance between France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom AG and their American partner Sprint Corp.

It said in a statement that the governments of France and Germany had fulfilled commitments regarding market opening and, therefore, its July conditional approval of the alliance became effective on December 1.

The key condition put by the Commission in July was that each government grant at least two licences for the construction or control of alternative nationwide telecoms infrastructure, such as those operated by railways and other utilities.
Germany did this in October and November 1996 and France had done likewise by the beginning of December, the statement published in the European Union's Official Journal said.
"(...) the exemptions (from EU competition rules) granted on July 17 1996 have taken effect on December 1 1996," it added.
The Commission's July decision followed two years of difficult negotiations on an early opening of the French and German telecoms markets.
The outcome was the liberalisation, ahead of the final breakdown of all telecoms monopolies in January 1, 1998, of so-called alternative networks from the middle of 1996.

The Global One joint venture effectively created in January last year was fiercely fought by rival telephone operators, mainly British Telecommunications Plc, which were worried about the two largest European companies pooling forces in the fast-developing market for new telecoms services.

It was one of the first global alliances to take up a position ready for the unprecedented wave of liberalism in the telecoms sector not just in Europe but also worldwide after the accord reached at the weekend at the World Trade Organisation.

Global One is also widely tipped to be seeking an Asian partner to be able to operate on a truly worldwise basis. Analysts say Britain's Cable and Wireless, which recently pulled out of its partnership with Germany's Veba AG and RWE, is a potential partner due to its significant interests in that side of the world.

The Commission is also currently carrying out an in-depth probe into the marriage between British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Corp of the United States although it is not expected to pose any significant problems as Britain has one of the most liberalised telecoms market.
